extensions.claim_text: Workhorse was one of five participants selected by the United States Postal Service (USPS) to build prototype vehicles for the USPS Next Generation Delivery Vehicle (NGDV) project, delivered six proto
extensions.source_label: USPS Office of Inspector General audit reports + USPS NGDV RFP records
extensions.endpoint_or_method: https://www.uspsoig.gov/document-library + USPS NGDV public RFP/SAM.gov solicitation history (Solicitation 6CAPSU-16-B-0007 family)
extensions.rationale: USPS does not buy through GSA/USAspending the way DoD/civil agencies do; USPS prototype contracts are administered internally. The OIG audit library and USPS-administered solicitation records are the canonical adjudicator for NGDV prototype-participant identity and contract scope.
extensions.expected_observable: list of NGDV prototype awardees; contract values; modification history
extensions.signal_direction: if WKHS is named as one of the 5 NGDV prototype awardees: corroborates; if absent or mis-scoped (e.g. listed as subcontractor only): contradicts the framing

extensions.signal_direction: co-bidder filings naming Workhorse corroborate; absence is non-informative

extensions.claim_text: Workhorse has received six separate orders totaling up to 1,405 vehicles from UPS under a Vehicle Purchase Agreement dated June 4, 2014; the sixth and most recent order is from Q1 2018.
extensions.source_label: UPS 10-K / 10-Q fulltext via EDGAR (CIK 0001090727)
extensions.rationale: Per H7 calibration, mega-cap fleet operators (UPS is mid-large cap, ~$120B) rarely disclose sub-material small-cap suppliers. But 1,405 vehicles at WKHS pricing is sub-material to UPS revenue — absence would be expected, not contradictory. Test anyway for context.
extensions.expected_observable: count of UPS filings mentioning 'Workhorse'
extensions.signal_direction: absent = baseline / non-informative; present = strong corroboration; ZERO mentions over 6+ years of orders would be informative absence given the 1,405-vehicle headline

extensions.claim_text: Workhorse has built and delivered approximately 360 electric and range-extended medium-duty delivery trucks cumulatively, and is the only American commercial electric vehicle OEM to achieve such a mil
extensions.source_label: NHTSA vPIC VIN decoder + IIHS Highway Loss Data Institute registrations
extensions.rationale: NHTSA vPIC registers every U.S. vehicle manufacturer with vehicle type classification ('Truck' vs 'Incomplete Vehicle'). A claimed 360 cumulative deliveries of medium-duty trucks implies ~360 WMI-registered VINs over 2015-2019. Currently NHTSA returns the manufacturer record but not per-year VIN counts — proposed extension would query IIHS HLDI for registration counts.
extensions.expected_observable: count of WKHS-WMI VINs registered by year; vehicle type
extensions.signal_direction: if registered count << 360 cumulative: contradicts production claim; if 'Incomplete Vehicle' rather than 'Truck': contradicts OEM framing

extensions.claim_text: Workhorse has built and delivered approximately 360 electric and range-extended medium-duty delivery trucks cumulatively, and is the only American commercial electric vehicle OEM to achieve such a mil
extensions.source_label: EPA Vehicle Certification database
extensions.rationale: EPA certifies every model-year of every road vehicle sold in the US. A 6-year history of EV-truck deliveries should appear as Workhorse-certified medium-duty model-year filings.
extensions.expected_observable: certified model-years by manufacturer; engine family designations
extensions.signal_direction: presence of multiple model-year certifications corroborates ongoing OEM; absence contradicts

extensions.claim_text: Workhorse has built and delivered approximately 360 electric and range-extended medium-duty delivery trucks cumulatively, and is the only American commercial electric vehicle OEM to achieve such a mil
extensions.source_label: CARB (California Air Resources Board) HVIP voucher records
extensions.rationale: CARB's Hybrid and Zero-Emission Truck Voucher Incentive Project (HVIP) lists every eligible electric truck by VIN; many WKHS deliveries plausibly used HVIP vouchers. A 360-unit cumulative delivery should leave a HVIP redemption trail.
extensions.expected_observable: voucher-redemption counts per manufacturer; eligible-vehicle catalog entries
extensions.signal_direction: voucher count << claim contradicts; matching count corroborates

extensions.claim_text: Workhorse owns a 250,000 square-foot truck assembly facility on 47 acres in Union City, Indiana with capacity to build up to 60,000 trucks per year, plus a 45,000 sq ft administration/R&D/manufacturin
extensions.source_label: OSHA Form 300A Establishment Search at the Union City and Loveland addresses
extensions.rationale: A 250,000 sq ft assembly plant with stated 60,000 truck/yr capacity implies a headcount far above the OSHA 300A 20-emp filing threshold. Absence at Union City would be a CLAIMED_LOCATION_GAP equivalent for industrial scale. (Note: WKHS later disclosed Union City had only ~100 employees in 2020 — a real plant but operating at a small fraction of stated capacity.)
extensions.expected_observable: establishment records, annual_average_employees, NAICS code
extensions.signal_direction: presence with low headcount (<200) = real-but-undersubscribed plant; absence = stronger contradiction; presence at Loveland but NOT Union City = HQ-only scope

extensions.claim_text: Workhorse owns a 250,000 square-foot truck assembly facility on 47 acres in Union City, Indiana with capacity to build up to 60,000 trucks per year, plus a 45,000 sq ft administration/R&D/manufacturin
extensions.source_label: BLS QCEW Randolph County IN (FIPS 18135) NAICS 3361 employment baseline
extensions.rationale: 60,000 trucks/yr is a stated CAPACITY (not delivery count). A facility actually operating at that scale would dominate Randolph County NAICS 3361 employment (population ~25k). Even at 10% utilization (i.e. 6,000 trucks/yr) the employment footprint would be ~500-1000 FTE — a plurality of the county's manufacturing workforce. QCEW data adjudicates the plausibility of the OPERATIONAL scale, separate from the legal-CAPACITY claim.
extensions.expected_observable: county+NAICS employment denominator
extensions.signal_direction: if claimed scale would represent <2% of county NAICS-3361 employment, capacity is dormant; >50% means real

extensions.claim_text: Workhorse owns a 250,000 square-foot truck assembly facility on 47 acres in Union City, Indiana with capacity to build up to 60,000 trucks per year, plus a 45,000 sq ft administration/R&D/manufacturin
extensions.source_label: Randolph County Indiana property tax assessor + Union City utility/water-tap records
extensions.endpoint_or_method: county-assessor portal (manual) + Indiana state environmental permit database
extensions.rationale: A 47-acre, 250,000 sqft owned assembly facility leaves a property-tax and state-environmental-permit footprint that is independent of EPA federal registries.
extensions.expected_observable: parcel ownership; assessed value; air/water permit holder
extensions.signal_direction: ownership match = corroborates physical existence (not operating scale); state permits = operational

extensions.claim_text: Workhorse's 2019 financial statements include a going-concern qualifier; the Company had an accumulated deficit of $178.8 million as of December 31, 2019, current liabilities exceeded current assets b
extensions.source_label: claim_evolution self-disclosure tracking on 'going concern' language
extensions.rationale: Distress-cluster fingerprints are temporal. Tracking whether 'going concern' language persists, intensifies, or disappears in 2020 10-Qs and subsequent 10-K filings is the canonical adjudicator of distress evolution.
extensions.expected_observable: count of filings mentioning going-concern; covenant references; subsequent-event disclosures
extensions.signal_direction: persistent language = chronic distress; disappearance = resolved (often via dilutive equity raise — which is itself a distress marker)

extensions.claim_text: Workhorse's 2019 financial statements include a going-concern qualifier; the Company had an accumulated deficit of $178.8 million as of December 31, 2019, current liabilities exceeded current assets b
extensions.source_label: SEC EDGAR S-3/S-1/424B prospectus supplement cadence
extensions.rationale: Shelf-registration draw-downs and ATM cadence are the operational fingerprint of micro-cap distress refinancing. 2019 alone shows Convertible Note $39M + Series B Pfd $25M + common $5.9M issuance — a textbook distress-cluster fingerprint per H10.
extensions.expected_observable: count of prospectus supplements; dollar amounts raised; pace acceleration
extensions.signal_direction: 3+ supplements in <12mo = elevated; pace acceleration = severe
